newsitem.title: DUBAI: Japan-UAE trade surges to record levels in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Japan-UAE trade surges to record levels in 1996.

text.p: Trade between Japan and the United Arab Emirates surged to an all-time high in 1996, rising 13 percent to $13.9 billion, official figures showed on Monday.
In 1995 the value of bilateral trade stood at $12.3 billion from $11.4 billion in 1994, the Japan External Trade Organisation (JETRO) said.
In yen terms, bilateral trade grew 30.2 percent in 1996.
Japanese exports to the UAE rose 10 percent to $2.31 billion in 1996, JETRO said. In yen terms, exports increased 27 percent.
Machinery and equipment constituted the major part of exports to the UAE and were worth $1.67 billion in 1996 from $1.53 billion in 1995, it said.

"The depreciation of the Japanese yen against the U.S. currency in recent times may help the Japanese products in the UAE market to become more competitive and thus enhance the prospects of a sustained growth in exports," JETRO said.
Japanese imports from the UAE rose by 13.4 percent in dollar terms and 30.8 percent in yen terms. The import value stood at $11.54 billion in 1996 from $10.17 billion in 1995.

Japan was the largest buyer of mineral fuels from the UAE, with imports valued at $11.34 billion in 1996. This accounted for more than 98 percent of total imports from the UAE. Crude oil alone constituted more than 80 percent of total imports.
A total of 449.4 million barrels of crude oil valued at $9.35 billion was imported from the UAE in 1996, compared to 449.3 million valued at $8.21 billion in 1995.
Some 28.2 percent of Japan's crude oil needs were met by the UAE in 1996.
The UAE was Japan's fifth largest supplier of natural gas in 1996, with imports valued at $707 million compared to $626 million in 1995, an increase of 12.9 percent, JETRO said.
"Though the exports to the UAE increased, the imports also shot up and the balance of trade was kept persistently high at more than $9 billion in favour of the United Arab Emirates."

Trade with the UAE accounted for 3.3 percent of Japan's global trade of $763.1 billion and 37 percent of Japan's $37.5 billion in trade with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, JETRO said. The GCC groups Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar.
